dataset.note: Historical statistics describe the 1999-2008 dataset (modelling cohort).

statistical_tests.caveat: Encounters from the same patient are not independent, so p-values are optimistic; use effect sizes (Cramér's V, rank-biserial) for ranking.

findings: 11,314 of 99,340 cohort encounters (11.4%) were readmitted within 30 days - a class imbalance of about 7.8:1, so accuracy alone would be misleading.
The readmission rate rises from 8.6% for patients with no inpatient stay in the prior year to 37.1% for those with 5+ prior stays.
Prior emergency visits show a similar gradient: 10.7% (none) vs 25.3% (3+ visits).
Among age brackets with at least 1,000 encounters, the rate ranges from 9.8% ([50-60)) to 14.3% ([20-30)).
Readmission is 8.4% after a 1-day stay and 13.5% after a 14-day stay.
Discharge destination matters: 'Rehab facility' has a 27.7% rate vs 'Home' at 9.3% (groups with ≥1,000 encounters).
HbA1c was not measured in 83% of encounters; readmission rate is 11.7% when untested vs 9.9% when >8%.
Encounters where insulin was adjusted (Up 13.3%, Down 14.2%) show higher rates than no insulin (10.2%).

By effect size, the categorical variable most associated with readmission is 'discharge_disposition' (Cramér's V = 0.115); all associations are weak individually, which foreshadows modest discrimination for any model on this dataset.

model.name: Gradient Boosting

risk_bands.name: Moderate
risk_bands.guidance: Around or modestly above the historical rate.

risk_bands.name: High
risk_bands.guidance: Roughly twice the historical rate or more.

model.selection_rule: Highest mean group-aware CV PR-AUC; ties (within 0.002) broken by higher ROC-AUC then lower Brier score. The test set is never used for selection.
model.threshold_strategy: Threshold maximising F2 (recall-weighted) on calibrated out-of-fold training predictions, restricted to flagging at most 40% of encounters; never tuned on the test set.
model.note: Model metrics are computed on a held-out, patient-disjoint test set.

evaluation.caveat: Retrospective, single-dataset evaluation (1999-2008 US hospitals). These metrics do not establish clinical usefulness or performance in any other population.

explainability.interpretation_note: SHAP values describe how the model's prediction depends on each input (predictive association learned from historical data). They are not causal effects: changing a feature in reality will not necessarily change risk.

baseline_drift.notes: 'latest_20pct_encounters' uses encounter_id order as a proxy for time; the public dataset has no dates, so this is an approximation of temporal drift. Those encounters overlap the training data, so it demonstrates the mechanism rather than a true prospective check.
